title: New Official Plan recommended for adoption
subtitle: Westmount and Auditorium heritage changes, Borden Avenue towers, Trussler subdivision update, Patricia Avenue school zone stopping ban
overview: The committee spent most of the evening on Kitchener 2051, the city's new Official Plan. It recommended that Council adopt the plan and forward it to the Province of Ontario for approval {{vote:m4}}. The plan would replace the 2014 Official Plan and remove the Region of Waterloo plan as it applies to Kitchener. It allows more housing types in every neighbourhood and directs the tallest buildings to strategic growth areas.

Before the final vote, the committee amended the plan. The Westmount and Auditorium neighbourhoods would be treated as heritage neighbourhoods with lower height limits. Several employment properties kept their existing permitted uses. Properties on Victoria Street North and Mill Street received different designations. Lands near Ottawa Street South in the Laurentian Hills area were moved from strategic growth area to neighbourhood designations. Staff will report back to Council on parkland and trails on June 29.

The committee also recommended approving two 51- and 57-storey towers at 50 Borden Avenue South {{vote:m3}}, changes to the Trussler Road subdivision plan and zoning {{vote:m2}}, and a weekday stopping ban on Patricia Avenue near a school {{vote:m1}}. Council makes the final decisions.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended that Council adopt the new Official Plan and related amendments, as amended at the meeting, and forward them to the Province for approval {{vote:m4}}.
The committee recommended changing the land use designation and zoning to allow a high-rise mixed-use development near the Borden LRT stop, and endorsing the urban design brief {{vote:m3}}.

decisions.item: 2219 Ottawa Street South and 808 Trussler Road subdivision
decisions.detail: The committee recommended modifying the draft plan and conditions of an approved subdivision and approving minor zoning changes to match the refined plans {{vote:m2}}.
The committee recommended prohibiting stopping from 8:00 am to 4:30 pm on weekdays on the south side of Patricia Avenue, west of Spadina Road West, and amending the Uniform Traffic Bylaw {{vote:m1}}.

debate: Delegates from the Westmount and Auditorium neighbourhoods asked for lower height limits and for each area to be treated as a single heritage neighbourhood. They said growth and heritage can coexist, with taller buildings on nearby main roads. Some councillors said these areas should be protected, and staff's modelling showed a small effect on housing numbers.

Housing advocacy groups supported the plan and urged the committee not to carve neighbourhoods out of intensification. They said heritage should not be used to limit housing. Another delegate said six-storey buildings in low-rise areas would cause privacy and overlook problems and suggested placing them on main streets instead.

Developers' planners and landowners asked for more flexible land uses, such as keeping existing employment and commercial permissions. Several of these requests were met through amendments. One delegate objected to the plan's parkland rules, which no longer count trails toward parkland dedication. Staff said dedication is meant for programmable parks, and some councillors said they wanted more clarity.

Other delegates raised the two-hectare exemption from the housing-mix policy, which they said could allow low-density greenfield development. They also raised institutional lands downtown, which were not redesignated, and tree canopy targets set by ward rather than neighbourhood. Staff said the exemption mainly applies to greenfield subdivisions and that the downtown lands were outside this review's scope. The canopy concern was referred to staff's tracking list.
